queries.sql: SELECT o.country, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_revenue_eur FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.country ORDER BY o.country

WITH line AS (
  SELECT o.order_id,
         (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS rev,
         CASE WHEN o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-04-01' THEN 'Q1_2025'
              WHEN o.order_date >= '2024-10-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-01-01' THEN 'Q4_2024'
         END AS qtr
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
  WHERE o.status = 'completed'
)
SELECT qtr, SUM(rev) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count, SUM(rev)/COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS avg_order_value
FROM line
WHERE qtr IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY qtr
ORDER BY qtr

SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS qtr, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS completed_orders FROM orders WHERE status='completed' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT COUNT(*) AS shipment_count FROM shipments s JOIN orders o ON s.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.country = 'Belgium'
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status

SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_ordered FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status='completed' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_quantity_ordered DESC

WITH line AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, oi.order_item_id, oi.quantity, COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0) AS qty_returned,
         oi.unit_price, oi.line_discount_pct, o.fx_rate_to_eur,
         date_trunc('quarter', o.order_date) AS qtr
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
  WHERE o.status='completed' AND o.country='France' AND o.order_date >= '2025-04-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-10-01'
)
SELECT qtr,
  SUM(quantity) AS gross_qty,
  SUM(qty_returned) AS returned_qty,
  SUM(qty_returned)*1.0/SUM(quantity) AS return_rate,
  SUM((quantity - qty_returned) * unit_price * (1-line_discount_pct) * fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_revenue,
  SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1-line_discount_pct) * fx_rate_to_eur) AS gross_revenue
FROM line GROUP BY qtr ORDER BY qtr

WITH line AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date,
         (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS rev
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
  WHERE o.status='completed' AND o.country='France' AND o.order_date >= '2025-07-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-10-01'
),
attributed AS (
  SELECT l.*, cs.segment
  FROM line l
  LEFT JOIN customer_segments cs ON cs.customer_id = l.customer_id
    AND cs.valid_from <= l.order_date AND (cs.valid_to IS NULL OR l.order_date < cs.valid_to)
)
SELECT segment, SUM(rev) AS revenue, SUM(rev)*1.0/SUM(SUM(rev)) OVER () AS share
FROM attributed GROUP BY segment ORDER BY segment

WITH line AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('quarter', o.order_date) AS qtr,
         (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) AS net_qty,

  FROM order_items oi

  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id

)
SELECT qtr, SUM(rev) AS revenue, SUM(net_qty) AS net_qty_sold, SUM(rev)/NULLIF(SUM(net_qty),0) AS avg_rev_per_unit, AVG(line_discount_pct) AS avg_discount_pct
FROM line GROUP BY qtr ORDER BY qtr

SELECT pp.product_id, p.name, pp.unit_price, pp.valid_from, pp.valid_to

WITH line AS (

    (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS rev,

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id), shipment_counts AS (SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_shipments FROM shipments GROUP BY order_id) SELECT sc.n_shipments, COUNT(*) FROM order_metrics om LEFT JOIN shipment_counts sc ON sc.order_id = om.order_id GROUP BY sc.n_shipments ORDER BY 1

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id), shipment_counts AS (SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_shipments FROM shipments GROUP BY order_id) SELECT CASE WHEN sc.n_shipments >= 2 THEN 'split (2+)' ELSE 'single' END AS fulfillment_type, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, AVG(om.revenue - om.net_cost) AS avg_profit_eur, AVG((om.revenue-om.net_cost)/NULLIF(om.revenue,0)) AS avg_margin FROM order_metrics om JOIN shipment_counts sc ON sc.order_id = om.order_id GROUP BY fulfillment_type ORDER BY fulfillment_type

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.country, o.order_date, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.country, o.order_date) SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost) AS total_profit, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM order_metrics GROUP BY country ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.country, o.order_date, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.country, o.order_date) SELECT (CASE WHEN country='Switzerland' THEN 'Switzerland' ELSE 'Eurozone' END) AS grp, date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS qtr, SUM(revenue) AS revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin, COUNT(*) AS n_orders FROM order_metrics GROUP BY grp, qtr ORDER BY qtr, grp

SELECT o.country, SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0))*1.0/SUM(oi.quantity) AS return_rate FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id=oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status='completed' GROUP BY o.country ORDER BY return_rate DESC
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS qtr, status, COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE country='France' GROUP BY qtr, status ORDER BY qtr, status

SELECT date_trunc('quarter', o.order_date) AS qtr, SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0))*1.0/SUM(oi.quantity) AS return_rate FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id=oi.order_item_id WHERE o.country='France' AND o.status='completed' GROUP BY qtr ORDER BY qtr

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date) SELECT c.customer_id, c.name, SUM(om.revenue) AS net_revenue_2025 FROM order_metrics om JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = om.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY net_revenue_2025 DESC LIMIT 10

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id), cust AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(revenue) AS revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM order_metrics GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT (CASE WHEN margin > 0.20 THEN '>20%' ELSE '<=20%' END) AS bucket, COUNT(*), MIN(margin), MAX(margin), AVG(margin) FROM cust GROUP BY bucket
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT oi.order_item_id, p.category, (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS revenue, (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS net_cost FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed') SELECT category, SUM(revenue) AS revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM order_metrics GROUP BY category ORDER BY margin DESC

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date), seg AS (SELECT om.*, cs.segment FROM order_metrics om JOIN customer_segments cs ON cs.customer_id = om.customer_id AND cs.valid_from <= om.order_date AND (cs.valid_to IS NULL OR om.order_date < cs.valid_to)) SELECT segment, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS n_customers, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, AVG(revenue) AS avg_order_value, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM seg GROUP BY segment

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty, SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) AS qty_returned, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id), cust AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, SUM(qty_returned)*1.0/SUM(qty) AS return_rate FROM order_metrics GROUP BY customer_id), current_seg AS (SELECT customer_id, segment FROM customer_segments WHERE valid_to IS NULL) SELECT cs.segment, COUNT(*) AS n_customers, AVG(c.n_orders) AS avg_orders, AVG(c.total_revenue) AS avg_revenue, AVG(c.return_rate) AS avg_return_rate FROM cust c JOIN current_seg cs ON cs.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY cs.segment

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id), cust AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost) AS total_profit, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM order_metrics GROUP BY customer_id), current_seg AS (SELECT customer_id, segment FROM customer_segments WHERE valid_to IS NULL) SELECT cs.segment, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(c.total_profit) AS avg_profit_per_customer, AVG(c.margin) AS avg_margin FROM cust c JOIN current_seg cs ON cs.customer_id=c.customer_id GROUP BY cs.segment

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty, SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) AS qty_ret FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_date), seg AS (SELECT om.*, cs.segment FROM order_metrics om JOIN customer_segments cs ON cs.customer_id = om.customer_id AND cs.valid_from <= om.order_date AND (cs.valid_to IS NULL OR om.order_date < cs.valid_to)) SELECT segment, SUM(qty_ret)*1.0/SUM(qty) AS return_rate, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS n_cust, COUNT(*)*1.0/COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS orders_per_customer FROM seg GROUP BY segment

WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty, SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) AS qty_ret, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id), cust AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, SUM(qty_ret)*1.0/SUM(qty) AS return_rate FROM order_metrics GROUP BY customer_id), current_seg AS (SELECT customer_id, segment FROM customer_segments WHERE valid_to IS NULL), stats AS (SELECT AVG(c.n_orders) FILTER (WHERE cs.segment='VIP') AS vip_orders, STDDEV(c.n_orders) AS sd_orders, AVG(c.total_revenue) FILTER (WHERE cs.segment='VIP') AS vip_rev, STDDEV(c.total_revenue) AS sd_rev, AVG(c.return_rate) FILTER (WHERE cs.segment='VIP') AS vip_ret, STDDEV(c.return_rate) AS sd_ret FROM cust c JOIN current_seg cs ON cs.customer_id=c.customer_id) SELECT cu.name, c.customer_id, c.n_orders, ROUND(c.total_revenue,0) AS revenue, ROUND(c.return_rate,4) AS return_rate, ROUND(SQRT(POWER((c.n_orders - s.vip_orders)/NULLIF(s.sd_orders,0),2) + POWER((c.total_revenue - s.vip_rev)/NULLIF(s.sd_rev,0),2) + POWER((c.return_rate - s.vip_ret)/NULLIF(s.sd_ret,0),2)),3) AS dist_to_vip_centroid FROM cust c JOIN current_seg cs ON cs.customer_id=c.customer_id JOIN customers cu ON cu.customer_id=c.customer_id CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE cs.segment='standard' ORDER BY dist_to_vip_centroid ASC LIMIT 10

WITH line AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, oi.order_item_id, oi.quantity, COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0) AS qty_returned,
         oi.unit_price, oi.line_discount_pct, o.fx_rate_to_eur,
         date_trunc('quarter', o.order_date) AS qtr
  FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id
  WHERE o.status='completed' AND o.country='France' AND o.order_date >= '2025-04-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-10-01'
)
SELECT qtr, SUM(quantity) AS gross_qty, SUM(qty_returned) AS returned_qty,
  SUM(qty_returned)*1.0/SUM(quantity) AS return_rate,
  SUM((quantity - qty_returned) * unit_price * (1-line_discount_pct) * fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_revenue,
  SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1-line_discount_pct) * fx_rate_to_eur) AS gross_revenue
FROM line GROUP BY qtr ORDER BY qtr
answers.answer: Net revenue in France fell from EUR 54,907 in Q2 2025 to EUR 29,998 in Q3 2025 (about -45%), but this was not a demand problem: gross (pre-return) revenue was essentially flat/slightly up (EUR 55,482 in Q2 vs EUR 56,531 in Q3), and order_date-based ordered quantity also held up (556 vs 606 units). The decline was driven almost entirely by a spike in returns: the France return rate jumped from about 1.3% of ordered quantity in Q2 2025 to about 45.9% in Q3 2025 (278 of 606 units returned). This matches the known Q3 2025 France fulfillment-delay anomaly, which drove a surge in partial product returns; because orders.status stays 'completed' regardless of later returns, the drop is only visible once returned quantity is netted out at the line-item level, not by looking at order status.

WITH line AS (
  SELECT o.country,
    (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS rev,
    (oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1 - oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur AS cost
  FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id=o.order_id
  LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id=oi.order_item_id
  WHERE o.status='completed'
)
SELECT 'ALL' AS scope, SUM(rev) AS revenue, SUM(cost) AS net_cost, (SUM(rev)-SUM(cost))/SUM(rev) AS margin FROM line
UNION ALL
SELECT country, SUM(rev), SUM(cost), (SUM(rev)-SUM(cost))/SUM(rev) FROM line GROUP BY country
answers.answer: Yes, essentially without limit from a margin-ratio standpoint, and there is currently a very large cushion either way. Overall company margin is about 54.9% (EUR 873,775 revenue, EUR 394,443 net cost) and France's own margin is about 55.0% (EUR 290,224 revenue, EUR 130,666 net cost) -- both far above the 20% floor, and France is only about a third of total revenue, so even a sharp France-specific change would move the overall ratio only modestly. More importantly, under Sahara's own accounting convention, deepening the discount on French orders would not move the margin ratio at all: line margin = (unit_price*(1-d) - unit_cost*(1-d))/(unit_price*(1-d)) = 1 - unit_cost/unit_price, which is mathematically independent of the discount rate d, because finance's policy discounts cost proportionally along with revenue (see discount_cost_policy.md). So increasing French discounts would reduce absolute revenue and profit euros, but would not by itself push the margin percentage below 20% -- it would stay at roughly today's ~55% no matter how deep the discount goes, all else equal. The real constraint on discounting is therefore revenue/profit dollars and competitive/behavioral effects (e.g. whether deeper discounts change purchase volume), not the margin ratio.

answers.sql: WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id), shipment_counts AS (SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_shipments FROM shipments GROUP BY order_id) SELECT CASE WHEN sc.n_shipments >= 2 THEN 'split (2+)' ELSE 'single' END AS fulfillment_type, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, AVG(om.revenue - om.net_cost) AS avg_profit_eur, AVG((om.revenue-om.net_cost)/NULLIF(om.revenue,0)) AS avg_margin FROM order_metrics om JOIN shipment_counts sc ON sc.order_id = om.order_id GROUP BY fulfillment_type ORDER BY fulfillment_type
answers.answer: Orders requiring split fulfillment (2+ shipments) are slightly MORE profitable on average than single-shipment orders, both in absolute profit and in margin. The difference in margin is small, so split fulfillment is not meaningfully less profitable; if anything orders needing multiple shipments tend to be larger/higher-value orders, which slightly increases both revenue and profit per order.

answers.sql: WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.country, o.order_date, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.country, o.order_date) SELECT country, SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM order_metrics GROUP BY country ORDER BY total_revenue DESC; -- plus quarterly trend by country and return_rate by country (see analysis)
answers.answer: No -- the data does not make a strong case for prioritizing Swiss expansion over the Eurozone markets. Margins are essentially the same everywhere: Switzerland 54.57%, France 54.98%, Germany 55.07%, Belgium 54.60% -- a spread of well under 1 percentage point, so CHF operations are not more profitable per euro of revenue than EUR operations. Switzerland is also the smallest market by revenue (EUR 158.8K total vs France EUR 290.2K, Germany EUR 258.9K, Belgium EUR 165.9K, i.e. only ~18% of total revenue across the four markets), and its quarterly revenue trend is flat-to-declining over the observed period (~EUR 30.5K in 2024-Q3 falling to ~EUR 22.9K in 2025-Q2, only partially recovering to ~EUR 27.1K by 2025-Q4), whereas the Eurozone markets combined show a generally higher and more resilient revenue base (the one dip, in 2025-Q3, is the known France fulfillment-delay/returns anomaly, not a systemic Eurozone weakness). On the positive side, Switzerland has a low return rate (3.76%, second-best after Belgium's 2.93%, well below France's anomaly-driven 10.86%), indicating good fulfillment quality there. Overall: comparable margin, weaker revenue growth momentum, smaller base, plus the added complexity/risk of a non-EUR currency -- the trends favor continuing to invest in the larger, comparably-profitable Eurozone markets over an aggressive Swiss expansion, though Switzerland's low return rate means it isn't a bad market either.

answers.sql: WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id), cust AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(revenue) AS revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin FROM order_metrics GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers, MIN(margin), MAX(margin), AVG(margin) FROM cust WHERE margin > 0.20
answers.answer: All 300 customers in the dataset could be offered a 10% discount and stay above 20% margin -- in fact, every customer already has a margin between 48.5% and 59.4% (average 54.8%), far above the 20% floor. Two things drive this: (1) at the current data, no customer's margin is anywhere close to 20%, so there is enormous headroom; and (2) under Sahara Retail's discount accounting convention (see discount_cost_policy.md), cost is booked proportionally to the same discount factor applied to revenue for margin purposes, i.e. margin = 1 - unit_cost/unit_price is invariant to discount depth -- granting an additional 10% discount scales both revenue and cost down together and does not erode the margin ratio at all under this convention. So mathematically, adding a 10% discount would leave every customer's margin unchanged from where it is today, and since every customer is already well above 20%, every customer qualifies. If a stricter interpretation is intended -- where the extra 10% discount is NOT proportionally offset in cost (i.e. it comes straight off current profit) -- the conclusion is unchanged here too: even a full 10-point margin hit would only bring the lowest-margin customer from ~48.5% down to ~38.5%, still comfortably above 20%. Either way: all 300 customers, across all four markets, qualify.

answers.sql: WITH order_metrics AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.country, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_price * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS revenue, SUM((oi.quantity - COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) * oi.unit_cost * (1-oi.line_discount_pct) * o.fx_rate_to_eur) AS net_cost, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty, SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity_returned,0)) AS qty_ret FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.country) SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, SUM(revenue) AS revenue, SUM(revenue-net_cost)/NULLIF(SUM(revenue),0) AS margin, SUM(qty_ret)*1.0/SUM(qty) AS return_rate FROM order_metrics GROUP BY country ORDER BY revenue DESC

Germany -- EUR 168,155 revenue, 55.11% margin, 3.55% return rate, 359 orders. Belgium -- EUR 101,911 revenue, 54.54% margin, 3.53% return rate, 237 orders. Switzerland -- EUR 100,682 revenue, 54.85% margin, 3.35% return rate, 215 orders. Recommendation: France should be the top priority to fix. Margins are essentially uniform across all four markets (54.5%-55.1%), so margin is not a differentiator, but France's 2025 return rate (14.24%) is roughly 4x every other market's (~3.3-3.6%), driven by a fulfillment-delay incident in 2025-Q3 that pushed that quarter's France return rate to 45.9% versus a 1-4% baseline in surrounding quarters. Even though France remains the largest and still-profitable market, this return-rate anomaly is actively eroding net revenue there (net revenue is reduced by returns even though orders.status stays 'completed') and is the clearest, most fixable operational problem in the portfolio -- exactly the kind of underperforming-market issue the reduce_return_rate_in_underperforming_markets priority is meant to catch. Germany, Belgium, and Switzerland all look healthy and comparable on both margin and return rate, so no urgent fix is indicated there.
